A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Minnow research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training and evaluation results for word classification, syntactic classification, generation, and BLiMP, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports aggregate human judgments and comparisons between human and GPT-4o evaluations in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The episodic next-token objective, shared placeholder token, language-modeling mixture, embedding-only Llama finetuning, and inference procedures are retained. Additional Llama-2 implementation information does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CHILDES, BabyLM-10M, MNLI-derived syntactic classification, Chimera, CoLLEGe-DefGen, Oxford, and BLiMP for the same tasks. The added human evaluation judges outputs from existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same Llama baselines, context-only control, CoLLEGe comparator, and specialized FLAN-T5 definition models. v3's expanded descriptions and syntactic summary table do not introduce additional comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the stated maximum sequence length for CHILDES finetuning with K=10 from 180 to 160 tokens in v3 Table 7; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. The new human protocol uses the first author to judge greedy and top-p outputs for 50 words each from BabyLM-10M and CoLLEGe-DefGen and all 33 Chimera words.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds aggregate human evaluation and human–GPT-4o judgment cross-tabulations to examine evaluator agreement and preference differences. This extends v2's selected author-judged examples; existing qualitative error analyses, semantic-coherence controls, and BLiMP checks are retained.

E5.justification: GPT-4o generation comparisons change from reporting seed 0 in v2 Appendix E to three-run averages with paired t-tests in v3 Tables 3 and 12. v3 also adds significance reporting for reference-based definition comparisons in Tables 4 and 23. This substantially expands statistical reporting; three-run training and uncertainty estimates for other experiments already existed in v2.

E6.justification: The head-to-head generation findings are substantially revised. For greedy Chimera generation, Minnow/baseline win percentages change from 55/42 to 42/53 for pretrained Llama-3 and from 36/52 to 48/44 for its instruction-tuned variant (v2 Table 1; v3 Table 3). These replace seed-0 reports with three-run averages, rather than establish cross-version model improvements. Human preference results and agreement counts are added, while classification, BLiMP, and reference-based definition scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation of episodes, conditional prediction, and likelihood-based classification is unchanged. New explanations of study and query examples do not introduce new formal definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: data-efficient word learning from human-scale input and improved few-shot word-learning capabilities through Minnow finetuning. Additional evaluation evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking baseline limitations to transient in-context learning and BabyLM syntactic performance to similarity with MNLI. Appendix E interprets human–GPT-4o disagreements as GPT-4o underestimating Minnow, while acknowledging the limited human evaluation. Generation and definition comparisons also receive more explicit significance qualifications.

D1.justification: v3 replaces a promised future code release with a concrete repository link. Appendix B newly specifies Llama-2's added tokens and model-specific learning rates in Table 7. Generation-table captions also identify the three-study-example condition used for definition comparisons. These disclosures do not establish corresponding changes to the underlying implementations.

R1.justification: v3 removes Bauer and Nation (1993), adds Moore and Bergelson (2024) to the morphology discussion, and gives the already-cited Anand et al. (2025) an additional explanatory role. The broader positioning relative to MetaICL and CoLLEGe remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits clarify likelihood-based classification, explain study/query terminology, standardize placeholder names, expand Appendix E, and correct wording and author affiliation information. The section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 2 illustrating an existing Appendix C example, Table 1 summarizing existing syntactic results, Table 7 presenting hyperparameters, and Tables 13–17 displaying human evaluations. Captions, significance bolding, and some table grouping change, but most existing visual material and the overall layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the generative evidence easier to assess through three-run aggregation and explicit significance reporting, including qualifications of numerical advantages. Clearer classification explanations and concrete code-access information also help readers. The small evaluation by the first author offers limited corroboration and limits the strength of the new claim that GPT-4o underestimates Minnow, so the overall improvement is modest.
